system_desc: Run system diagnostics. Output appears in the panel below.
network_desc: View network status and manage configuration.
ctrl_net_diag_desc: View detailed interface and port information.
ctrl_ipconfig_desc: Assign a static IP or revert to DHCP. Changes are written to /etc/dhcpcd.conf and take effect after a reboot.
ctrl_hostname_desc: Rename this device on the network. Only letters, numbers, and hyphens are allowed.
ctrl_smb_desc: Control the Samba file sharing service (smbd).
tunnels_desc: Manage remote access tunnels. Enabling a tunnel exposes this device beyond the local network.
ctrl_tailscale_desc: Join or leave the Tailscale network. Allows secure remote access via a private VPN mesh.
ctrl_ngrok_desc: Expose local ports to the internet via ngrok tunnelling. Auth token must be configured on the device first.
ctrl_newt_desc: Open-source alternative to ngrok. Connects this device to your Pangolin server over a secure WireGuard tunnel. Create a Site in Pangolin to get a Newt ID and secret.
docker_desc: Monitor and control Docker containers running on this device.
docker_overview_desc: View running containers, available images, and live resource usage.
docker_manage_desc: Enter a container name then choose an action. Logs shows the last 100 lines.
docker_run_desc: Pull an image and start a new container. All fields are validated before the command runs.
llama_desc: Run a language model on this device. Off by default so it uses no memory.
ctrl_llama_enable_desc: Starts the llama service. The rest of the panel keeps working either way.
ctrl_llama_model_desc: Paste the download link of a .gguf file from Hugging Face, then download it to this device.
llama_installed_empty: No models installed yet. Download one above.
chat_greeting: Hello! I'm your Xerxes Pi assistant. How can I help you manage your server today?
i2c_desc: Manage devices connected over the I2C bus.
oled_power_desc: Shows the chosen information on the OLED screen. When off, the screen is blank. Stays as set after a restart.
oled_state_idle_hint: Not in use: the display is only driven while it is on.
oled_content_desc: Choose what the screen shows. The preview updates as you make changes. Press Save to send them to the display.
oled_mode_qr: QR code to this admin panel
oled_content_saved: Saved. The display will update in a few seconds.
oled_content_saved_offline: Saved. The display will show this once it is reconnected.
oled_settings_desc: Which I2C bus and address the OLED is on. The defaults suit the 128x64 SSD1306 on the Xerxes Pi's Qwiic port. Some panels use 0x3D instead.
oled_err_no_bus: I2C bus {device} was not found. Check that I2C is enabled (raspi-config → Interface Options → I2C).
oled_err_no_device: The display did not respond at {address} on {device}. Power off the Pi, then check the Qwiic cable and the address.
oled_err_write_failed: Lost contact with the display. Your settings are kept and will be shown again once it reconnects.
oled_err_unsupported: This build cannot drive the display (it needs Linux with I2C). The preview still works.
oled_err_probe_timeout: The display did not respond in time.
oled_err_invalid_stat: One of the chosen items is not supported.
oled_err_no_stats: Choose at least one item to show.
oled_err_invalid_bus: I2C bus must be a number from 0 to 1023.
oled_err_invalid_address: I2C address must be from 0x03 to 0x77.
oled_err_save_failed: Could not save the settings. The change applies until the backend restarts.
rfid_reader_desc: When on, tapping a registered tag runs its command on this device with the backend's privileges (root when deployed). Unknown tags are logged and ignored. Stays on after a restart.
rfid_tags_empty: No tags registered. Add one below.
rfid_add_desc: Scan a tag on the reader (or type its ID), then enter the command to run when it is tapped.
rfid_live_desc: Shows every tag held to the reader, whether it is registered, and the raw read details. Live scan itself never runs commands; the reader still does if it is on.
rfid_live_empty: Start a live scan, then place tags near the reader.
rfid_settings_desc: Which I2C bus and address the RFID module is on, and where tags are stored. The defaults suit the PiicoDev module on a Xerxes Pi. I2C must be enabled (raspi-config → Interface Options → I2C).
